## Appendix D Task Description

The following Table [7](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#A4.T7 "Table 7 ‣ Appendix D Task Description ‣ Language Modeling for the Future of Finance: A Quantitative Survey into Metrics, Tasks, and Data Opportunities") and Table [8](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#A4.T8 "Table 8 ‣ Appendix D Task Description ‣ Language Modeling for the Future of Finance: A Quantitative Survey into Metrics, Tasks, and Data Opportunities") describe the task description with examples.

| | | | --- | --- | | Primary Task | Examples & Insights | | Finance-Related (Categories IV) | | | Explainable AI (XAI) refers to methods that make machine learning outputs more interpretable and less of a "black box." | These papers show how small input changes can drastically affect model explanations ([Sinha et al. 2021](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib94)) and highlight the instability of tools like LIME in sensitive applications ([Burger et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib12)). In finance, where decisions must be traceable and justifiable, clear and reliable explanation methods are essential for building trust in tasks like fraud detection and risk assessment. | | Privacy-preserving methods protect sensitive data while still allowing model training and analysis. | Examples include homomorphic encryption for text similarity ([Kim et al. 2022](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib51)), federated learning for distributed training without raw data exchange ([Zhao et al. 2024d](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib122)), and domain adaptation that shares only model parameters ([Xiao et al. 2024b](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib109)). These methods are especially important in finance, where institutions must work with private data while staying compliant and avoiding breaches. | | Numerical reasoning involves working with numbers and structured data to solve problems or develop algorithms. | This includes solving math word problems using declarative knowledge ([Roy & Roth 2018](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib84)), learning numeracy through number embeddings ([Duan et al. 2021](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib25)), and pretraining models for verifying tabular claims ([Akhtar et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib6)). In finance, good numerical reasoning supports tasks like market prediction and risk evaluation by improving how models interpret and reason about numbers. | | Financial Applications (Category III) | | | Sentiment analysis helps assess market mood and forecast financial movements using sources like news, social media, and reports. | Studies analyze opinions in reports and news ([Rodriguez Inserte et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib83)), investor sentiment on social media ([Guo et al. 2023a](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib33)), and tone in financial texts ([Choe et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib20)). As markets become more influenced by public opinion, sentiment analysis plays a growing role in trading and analysis. | | Information extraction (IE) and relation extraction focus on identifying entities and linking them to events or other entities. | Examples include extracting financial events from documents ([Zheng et al. 2019](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib123)), signals in reports ([Huang et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib37)), and patterns in social media ([Conforti et al. 2022](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib21)). These tools help connect companies, individuals, and financial instruments to real-world developments ([Liou et al. 2021](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib61)), supporting real-time analysis and prediction. | | Question Answering (QA) enables systems to find specific information in financial documents, reports, and databases. | QA models support quick access to relevant facts ([Mavi et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib72)), and recent work focuses on calibrating large language models (LLMs) for finance-specific tasks ([Zhao et al. 2024c](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib121); [Theuma & Shareghi 2024](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib98); [Addlesee 2024](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib3)). This area emphasizes not only building QA tools but also improving their accuracy for use in high-stakes financial contexts. |

| | | | --- | --- | | Primary Task | Examples & Insights | | Financial Resources (Category II) | | | Dataset and Resource Construction involves building structured, labeled financial datasets for model development and evaluation. | These papers focus on creating large-scale annotated resources ([Chen et al. 2020a](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib13)), including datasets like Tab-CQA ([Liu et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib62)) and ConvFinQA ([Chen et al. 2022c](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib19)) designed for reasoning over tables and multi-step numerical queries. Other works assemble corpora from Earnings calls ([Pardawala et al. 2025](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib81)), financial reports ([Shah et al. 2022](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib93)), company filings ([Zmandar et al. 2022](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib126)), news ([Tang et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib97)), and government documents ([Shah et al. 2023](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib92)), enabling downstream tasks like entity linking, numerical reasoning, or forecasting. | | Fraud detection leverages domain-specific data and models to identify deceptive financial behavior across platforms. | [Erben & Waldis 2024](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib28) identifies financial scams on Instagram using a fine-tuned BERT model deployed via browser extension and REST API. Another approach detects identity fraud through interactive dialogue, employing knowledge graphs and reinforcement learning to expose inconsistencies in claimed personal data ([Wang et al. 2019](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib105)). These systems highlight how NLP architectures can protect users from financial manipulation. | | Financial Forecast (Category I) | | | Stock Price and Volatility Prediction aims to forecast stock movements or market instability using text data. | These models use historical data ([Sawhney et al. 2021a](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib88)), news ([Ahbali et al. 2022](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib5)), and event-driven signals ([Sawhney et al. 2020a](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib86); [Wu 2020](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib107)) to predict stock trends. Volatility prediction further explores market sensitivity by analyzing unstructured text like press releases or financial articles ([Qin & Yang 2019](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib82)), helping traders anticipate fluctuations. | | Risk Prediction involves identifying the likelihood and impact of adverse financial events, such as defaults or market disruptions. | These models analyze unstructured data like earnings call transcripts ([Sang & Bao 2022](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib85)), regulatory filings, and legal documents to detect early signals of financial risk ([Li et al. 2023b](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib57)). Applications include credit risk estimation, fraud detection, and systemic risk monitoring ([Zhang et al. 2024](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib118)). |

## Appendix G Glossary

| Metric | Definition | | --- | --- | | Sharpe Ratio | Measures how much return an investment gives for each unit of risk, compared to a risk-free asset ([Investopedia Staff 2025a](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib41)). | | Maximum Drawdown | The biggest drop from a peak to a low point in a portfolio’s value before it recovers ([Investopedia Staff 2023b](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib40)). | | Cumulative Return | The total profit or loss from an investment over time ([Investopedia Staff 2023a](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2504.07274#bib.bib39)). |
